sections.overview: This small crambid moth is rare and very local in Belgium, where it has not been recorded since around 1920.
sections.identification: It belongs to the moth genus Pyrausta.
sections.habitat: It is associated with chalk and limestone soils and coastal dunes in the Belgian account.
sections.diet: The larvae feed mainly on mint and oregano; thyme is also listed as a host plant.
sections.behavior: Adults are recorded from late April into August, with two generations a year in the Belgian account.
sections.reproduction: No species-specific reproductive details were given in the consulted sources.
sections.ecology: The Belgian catalogue reports a decline across Western Europe, in addition to the species’ very local Belgian status.
sections.conservation: The cited rarity and decline are regional records, not a global conservation assessment.
